1	# E-01 — Layer System
2	
3	## Definition-completeness gate (run 2026-09-10)
4	
5	| Check | Result |
6	|---|---|
7	| Every story has at least one Given/When/Then rule with concrete values | Yes, 11 stories, 34 rules. Rules that depend on an open flag cite it inline. |
8	| Every input listed with range and rejection behavior | Yes, see Inputs. Two rejection behaviors are open (Q-002-02, Q-003-01). |
9	| Every output listed with where it is observable | Yes, see Outputs. On-screen elevation is open (Q-E01-01). |
10	| Implied-but-unstated behavior turned into flags | 14 new flags raised, Q-001-01 through Q-009-01. |
11	| Every visible-surface story has a reference | **No — by design a Godot design phase, not a screenshot pull.** `references/E-01/notes.md` records the plan: basic single-layer movement ships first, then Claude builds several interactive layer-system options in Godot for Westley to choose between; the choice fills the references. Blocks S-009, S-010, S-006 until then. |
12	| "Obviously working" in 60 seconds named | Yes, see below. |
13	
14	**Gate verdict: not passed.** Blocked on 15 open flags (Q-E01-01 plus 14 new) and on references. Stories are Spec'd, not Ready.
15	
16	## Purpose
17	
18	The layer system is the game's strategic defining characteristic. The battlefield is not a flat plane. It is a stack of three to five vertical layers, and a unit is always on exactly one of them. Terrain blocks layers at specific places, so a force can go over an obstacle on a high layer or around it on a low one. Vision across layers is worse than vision on your own layer, so a force on a layer you cannot see is a threat you do not know about. Changing layers costs time and leaves the unit briefly vulnerable.
19	
20	The promise this keeps for the player (vision_v2 Q6): a smaller force that understands surrounds, high ground, and layers beats a larger force that does not. Every rule below exists to make that promise testable.
21	
22	Era-agnostic: the engine knows "layers 1 and 2 are blocked here." The era pack decides whether that is an asteroid, a mountain, or a reef. Launch ships the Settled Reach with no per-unit-type layer restrictions.
23	
24	## Obviously working in 60 seconds
25	
26	Spawn a Raider and a Bastion on layer 3 next to a tall obstacle. Order both to layer 5. The Raider rises visibly within a second, the Bastion takes several seconds, and each unit's ring changes color when its layer changes. Place an enemy on layer 1 under the obstacle: neither unit sees it. Move an enemy onto layer 4 within half the Raider's sensor range: the Raider sees it, the Bastion does not until it is closer. Fire a pulse: the layer-1 enemy appears for two seconds, then vanishes. Order the Raider to layer 1 through the obstacle: it does not change layer until it moves clear of the blocked zone, then drops.
27	
28	## Stories
29	
30	### S-001 — The map decides where each layer is open
31	As a commander, I want terrain to block specific layers at specific places, so that going over, going around, and hiding in the blocked layers are real choices.
32	
33	Rules
34	- R-001-01  Given a map position where layers 1 and 2 are blocked and layers 3 to 5 are open, When any unit on layer 1 or 2 is ordered to move through that position, Then its path avoids the blocked area on its current layer and the unit never occupies the blocked position on layers 1 or 2.
35	- R-001-02  Given the same position, When a unit on layer 3 moves through it, Then the unit passes straight through with no detour.
36	- R-001-03  Given a position where every layer is open, When any unit moves through it, Then no layer restriction applies.
37	- R-001-04  Given any map generated for any era pack, When the map is queried for layer accessibility at every sampled position and layer, Then the answer is a binary open or blocked per layer, and the count of layers is the same for every position on that map.
38	
39	Inputs: map layer accessibility mask (binary per layer per position); unit position; unit current layer.
40	Outputs: unit path; unit position over time; layer accessibility query result.
41	Open flags: Q-001-01 (layer count per map), Q-001-02 (which end is layer 1), Q-001-03 (no route on current layer).
42	
43	### S-002 — Hard layer transfer
44	As a commander, I want to order selected units to a specific layer, so that I can commit a force to a height when timing matters.
45	
46	Rules
47	- R-002-01  Given a selected unit on layer 3 at a position where layer 5 is open, When the player issues a hard transfer to layer 5, Then the unit begins its transition on the same tick and finishes on layer 5 after its transition duration (S-004).
48	- R-002-02  Given a selected unit at a position where layer 5 is blocked, When the player issues a hard transfer to layer 5, Then the unit keeps executing its current orders on its current layer, and begins the transition on the first tick it occupies a position where layer 5 is open.
49	- R-002-03  Given a unit with a pending hard transfer, When the player issues a second hard transfer to a different layer, Then the first transfer is discarded and only the second is pending.
50	- R-002-04  Given a unit with a pending hard transfer, When the player issues a move order, Then the transfer stays pending; a move order never clears a transfer.
51	- R-002-05  Given a hard transfer to the unit's current layer, When it is issued, Then it is accepted and completes immediately with no transition and no vulnerability window.
52	- R-002-06  Given a hard transfer to a layer outside the map's layer range, When it is issued, Then it is rejected and the unit's state does not change.
53	- R-002-07  Given a hard transfer order for a mixed selection, When it is issued, Then every unit in the selection gets its own pending transfer and each resolves independently by its own position and duration.
54	
55	Inputs: layer command (target layer, integer in map range); selection (1 to N units); unit position; accessibility mask.
56	Outputs: per-unit pending transfer; per-unit layer field in the tick delta; transition start and end events.
57	Open flags: Q-002-01 (non-adjacent target passes through intermediates or not), Q-002-02 (pending transfer never expires, or expires on arrival at the move destination).
58	
59	### S-003 — Layer preference
60	As a commander, I want to give units a standing preference for a layer, so that a scouting group stays high and a siege group stays low without me re-ordering them at every obstacle.
61	
62	Rules
63	- R-003-01  Given a selected unit with no preference, When the player sets preference to layer 2, Then the unit's preference is 2 and it begins a transition to layer 2 on the first tick it is at a position where layer 2 is open and it is not already on layer 2.
64	- R-003-02  Given a unit with preference 2 currently on layer 4 because layer 2 is blocked here, When the unit moves to a position where layer 2 is open, Then it begins its transition to layer 2 on that tick without a new order.
65	- R-003-03  Given a unit with preference 2 at a position where layer 2 is blocked, When any number of ticks pass, Then the unit continues its current orders on its current layer and never stalls or stops to wait.
66	- R-003-04  Given a unit with preference 2, When the player issues a hard transfer to layer 4, Then the preference is cleared and the hard transfer proceeds.
67	- R-003-05  Given a unit with preference 2, When the player issues the clear-preference action, Then the preference is cleared and the unit stays on its current layer.
68	- R-003-06  Given a unit with preference 2, When the player sets preference 3, Then the preference is 3 and any pending transition toward 2 is replaced.
69	- R-003-07  Given the modifier key held, When the player presses 1 through 5, Then that is a preference assignment, not a control-group recall; and Given the modifier key released, When the player presses 1 through 5, Then that is the standard control-group recall.
70	- R-003-08  Given a saved mission, When it is loaded, Then every unit's preference is restored exactly.
71	
72	Inputs: preference command (layer integer or clear); modifier key state; selection.
73	Outputs: per-unit preferred layer in the tick delta; preference indicator on screen (S-009); save file.
74	Open flags: Q-003-01 (modifier key default and clear-preference input).
75	
76	### S-004 — Changing layers takes time and leaves you exposed
77	As a commander, I want a layer change to cost time that depends on the unit type, so that hopping layers is a commitment and not a free dodge.
78	
79	Rules
80	- R-004-01  Given a Raider ordered from layer 3 to layer 4 at an open position, When the transition starts, Then the unit is on layer 4 exactly one transition duration later, with the duration taken from the unit type's transition time [Q-004-01 for the confirmed numbers; current config: Raider 1.0 s, Interceptor 1.2 s, Vanguard 2.5 s, Warden 2.0 s, Bombard 4.0 s, Bastion 5.0 s].
81	- R-004-02  Given a unit mid-transition, When any unit on its old layer would otherwise attack it, Then the attack does not target it, and the transitioning unit itself cannot attack.
82	- R-004-03  Given two units of different types ordered to the same layer at the same tick, When the faster type completes, Then the slower type is still mid-transition, and completion order always matches transition-time order.
83	- R-004-04  Given a unit mid-transition, When a new hard transfer to another layer is issued, Then the unit completes the current transition first and the new transfer becomes pending.
84	- R-004-05  Given the same seed and the same command stream, When the mission runs twice, Then every transition starts and ends on the same tick both times.
85	
86	Inputs: unit type transition time (per type, config); transition start tick.
87	Outputs: unit layer field; transitioning flag in the tick delta; attack eligibility.
88	Open flags: Q-004-01 (confirm durations), Q-004-02 (movement and new-layer targeting during the window).
89	
90	### S-005 — Seeing across layers is worse than seeing on your own
91	As a commander, I want cross-layer vision to shrink with layer distance, so that a force on a layer I am not watching is a real threat.
92	
93	Rules
94	- R-005-01  Given an observer with sensor radius 1,000 on layer 3 and an enemy on layer 3 at distance 900, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is in the observer's visible set.
95	- R-005-02  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 4 at distance 400, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is visible (adjacent layer factor 0.50, effective radius 500).
96	- R-005-03  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 4 at distance 600, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is not visible.
97	- R-005-04  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 5 at distance 150, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is visible (two-layer factor 0.20, effective radius 200); at distance 250 it is not.
98	- R-005-05  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 1 (two layers below) or any layer three or more away, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is never visible by passive detection at any distance.
99	- R-005-06  Given an observer standing at a vantage node, When the same enemies are placed, Then the adjacent factor is 1.00, the two-layer factor is 0.40, and a three-layer enemy is visible at factor 0.20.
100	- R-005-07  Given an observer inside a sensor interference zone of intensity 0.5, When an enemy is on an adjacent layer, Then the effective cross-layer radius is sensor radius × 0.50 × 0.50.
101	- R-005-08  Given fog on, When an enemy on another layer is outside the effective cross-layer radius, Then it is hidden from the player exactly as a same-layer enemy outside sensor radius is hidden: no silhouette, no marker, no special treatment.
102	
103	Inputs: observer layer, position, sensor radius; target layer, position; vantage membership; interference intensity at observer position.
104	Outputs: per-unit visible set in the tick delta; player-visible unit list; fog reveal on screen.
105	Open flags: Q-005-01 (what counts as standing at a vantage node).
106	
107	### S-006 — Sensor pulse
108	As a commander, I want to spend a pulse to see every layer around a unit for a moment, so that scouting before a commitment is a decision with a cost.
109	
110	Rules
111	- R-006-01  Given a pulse-capable unit with its pulse ready, When the player triggers the pulse, Then every enemy on every layer within the pulse radius is in the player's visible set for the next 2.0 seconds of sim time (40 ticks at 20 ticks per second).
112	- R-006-02  Given a pulse that started 2.0 seconds ago, When the next tick runs, Then enemies revealed only by the pulse leave the visible set.
113	- R-006-03  Given a pulse fired on tick T, When the player tries again before tick T plus 20.0 seconds (400 ticks), Then the command is rejected and the cooldown is unchanged.
114	- R-006-04  Given the pulse-capable unit is inside an interference zone of intensity 0.5, When it pulses, Then the pulse radius is halved.
115	- R-006-05  Given a pulse reveals an enemy on layer 1 while the observer is on layer 5, When the pulse expires and no passive detection applies, Then the enemy is hidden again.
116	
117	Inputs: pulse command; pulse-capable unit; pulse radius (config); cooldown state.
118	Outputs: pulse active flag and remaining cooldown in the tick delta; revealed set; cooldown ring on the HUD; visible pulse effect on screen.
119	Open flags: Q-006-01 (which units pulse, radius, and whether the pulse is the unit's one ability), Q-006-02 (last-seen markers after expiry).
120	
121	### S-007 — Cover blocks sight by height
122	As a commander, I want a tall obstacle to hide units on more layers than a short one, so that where I put a force relative to terrain changes what the enemy can see.
123	
124	Rules
125	- R-007-01  Given an obstacle whose height reaches layer 2 between an observer and a target both on layer 1, When one tick passes, Then the target is not visible.
126	- R-007-02  Given the same obstacle and both units on layer 3, When one tick passes, Then the target is visible (the obstacle does not reach layer 3).
127	- R-007-03  Given a target hidden behind cover, When it attacks an observer that cannot see it, Then the attack lands and the target stays hidden; firing never reveals.
128	- R-007-04  Given a target visible despite nearby cover, When it takes damage, Then damage is unmodified; cover is never a damage reduction.
129	- R-007-05  Given cover in a unit's path, When it moves, Then movement is unaffected; cover never blocks movement.
130	
131	Inputs: obstacle position, radius, height; observer and target positions and layers.
132	Outputs: visible set; damage applied; unit path.
133	Open flags: none beyond Q-001-01 (obstacle height thresholds depend on the layer count and spacing).
134	
135	### S-008 — Combat across layers
136	As a commander, I want to know whether a unit can shoot at an enemy one layer above it, so that layer position is a positional decision and not a guess.
137	
138	Rules
139	- R-008-01  Given an attacker on layer 3 and a visible enemy on layer 3 in range, When the attacker is idle or attack-moving, Then it engages.
140	- R-008-02  Given an attacker on layer 3 and a visible enemy on layer 4 in range, When the attacker is idle or attack-moving, Then [Q-008-01 decides: it does not engage (current code), or it engages with a stated range or damage modifier].
141	- R-008-03  Given a Bombard's area attack centered on layer 3, When enemies stand on layers 2 and 4 inside the radius, Then [Q-008-01 decides whether they take damage].
142	
143	Inputs: attacker layer, target layer, range, visibility.
144	Outputs: attack events; HP changes in the tick delta.
145	Open flags: Q-008-01 (prototype: same-layer only), Q-008-02 (the cross-layer damage and vision design and its research program; the game's most important undefined mechanic).
146	
147	### S-009 — I can see what layer every unit is on
148	As a commander, I want to see at a glance which layer each unit is on and which layer I am focused on, so that I never have to guess who can see whom.
149	
150	Rules
151	- R-009-01  Given any unit on screen, When the player looks at it, Then a ring under the unit shows one color per layer, and the color changes on the tick the unit's layer changes.
152	- R-009-02  Given a unit toggled toward another layer, When the player looks at it, Then the target disc on its spindle (R-009-05) gains an outline and a chevron, a waypoint-like mark of where it is going, distinct from the lit current-layer disc.
153	- R-009-05  Given any unit on screen, When drawn, Then a thin rod beside it carries five small discs, one per layer, the unit's own disc lit at about 50 percent, adjacent discs at 10 to 20 percent, discs two away at 5 percent (the Floor Spindle); and its grid tiers are flat discs that tilt to the ground's slope at each layer's height (Terrace Reading). Both are subdued, never loud, and never block the view of the battlefield behind them.
154	- R-009-06  Given units hidden from the player by the current perspective (behind terrain or another layer's ground), When the player looks at the scene, Then something tells them they are not seeing the whole picture [Q-009-02: the mechanism, such as a small mark on the occluding units].
155	- R-009-03  Given the layer strip on the HUD, When the player clicks a layer or presses Tab, Then the focused layer changes and the strip highlights the new one.
156	- R-009-04  Given the same selection and camera, When a T2 screenshot is taken, Then the ring colors match the sim's per-unit layer field for every unit in view.
157	
158	Inputs: unit layer, preferred layer; focus click or Tab.
159	Outputs: ring color per unit; spindle and terrace discs; target mark; focused layer on the strip.
160	Open flags: Q-009-02 (the occlusion indicator). Q-009-01 is closed: focus is purely visual, other layers dim slightly. Look chosen through the options pass, `docs/northstar/research/options/layer-system/`, Q-E01-08; Godot renders of it fill `references/E-01/notes.md`.
161	
162	### S-010 — Layers read as height on screen
163	As a commander, I want a unit on a higher layer to sit visibly higher than one on a lower layer, so that the layer stack reads as a stack and not as a color code.
164	
165	Rules
166	- R-010-01  Given a unit on layer L at position (x, y), When it is drawn, Then its world-space height is the layer's elevation from the map's layer mapping [Q-E01-01 decides where the mapping lives; current code: three z-bands 0 to 30, 30 to 100, 100 to 300 for a five-layer count, which is itself a defect].
167	- R-010-02  Given a unit transitioning from layer 3 to 4, When frames render during the transition, Then its drawn height moves from layer 3's elevation to layer 4's over the transition duration, not as a snap.
168	- R-010-03  Given a fixed camera and a unit ordered up one layer, When a T2 screenshot is taken before and after, Then the unit's screen position differs vertically by more than 5 percent of the viewport height.
169	
170	Inputs: layer to elevation mapping; camera.
171	Outputs: unit world position on screen.
172	Open flags: Q-E01-01. Reference required: `references/E-01/notes.md`, missing.
173	
174	### S-011 — Era packs may restrict unit types to layers
175	As an era designer, I want an era pack to say which layers a unit type may occupy, so that a submarine era or a ground-only era works on the same engine without code changes.
176	
177	Rules
178	- R-011-01  Given the Settled Reach era pack (no restriction mask), When any unit type is ordered to any open layer, Then it is accepted.
179	- R-011-02  Given an era pack whose mask permits type X on layers 4 and 5 only, When a type-X unit is ordered to layer 2, Then the order is rejected and the unit stays on its layer.
180	- R-011-03  Given the same pack, When a type-X unit spawns, Then it spawns on a permitted layer.
181	- R-011-04  Given the same pack, When a type-X unit has preference 2, Then the preference is rejected at assignment time.
182	
183	Inputs: era pack restriction mask (per unit type, set of layers; absent means unrestricted).
184	Outputs: command acceptance; spawn layer.
185	Open flags: none. Launch scope: capability present, mask absent (A-294, A-321).
186	
187	## Inputs
188	
189	| Input | Source | Range | Rejection |
190	|---|---|---|---|
191	| Layer accessibility mask | Map generator | Binary per layer per sampled position | Not player-issued |
192	| Layer count | Map or engine | 3 to 5 [Q-001-01] | Map generation fails outside range |
193	| Hard transfer | Player | Target layer in map range, selection 1 to N | Out of range: rejected, no state change. Era mask forbids: rejected |
194	| Preference set | Player | Layer in map range or clear | Same as hard transfer |
195	| Modifier key | Player | Held or released | None |
196	| Pulse | Player | Pulse-capable selected unit, cooldown ready | On cooldown or not capable: rejected |
197	| Unit type transition time | Config | 1.0 to 5.0 s [Q-004-01] | Not player-issued |
198	| Sensor radius, vantage membership, interference intensity | Sim | Per unit, per position | Not player-issued |
199	| Era restriction mask | Era pack | Per unit type, subset of layers, or absent | Malformed pack fails to load |
200	
201	## Outputs
202	
203	| Output | Observable where |
204	|---|---|
205	| Unit layer | Tick delta unit entry; ring color on screen; save file |
206	| Preferred layer | Tick delta unit entry; preference indicator; save file |
207	| Transitioning flag and remaining time | Tick delta unit entry; drawn height mid-tween |
208	| Visible set per unit; player-visible list | Tick delta; fog reveal on screen |
209	| Pulse active, cooldown remaining | Tick delta; HUD cooldown ring; pulse effect on screen |
210	| Command rejections | Command acknowledgement in the tick delta with a reason code |
211	| Focused layer | HUD strip highlight |
212	
213	## Invariants
214	
215	- A unit is on exactly one layer at every tick, including mid-transition (it is on its old layer until the transition completes).
216	- No unit ever occupies a position and layer the mask marks blocked.
217	- Visible set is symmetric in rule, not in outcome: A sees B does not imply B sees A.
218	- Same seed and command stream produce identical layer, visibility, and transition traces.
219	- Cover never changes damage or movement.
220	
221	## Scale requirements
222	
223	Numbers to be confirmed by Westley in Stage 3. Proposed: 1,000 units computing cross-layer visibility against 1,000 units in under 2 ms per tick; 10,000 units in under 20 ms per tick; accessibility queries at 10,000 per tick in under 1 ms.
224	
225	## Look and behavior references
226	
227	`references/E-01/notes.md`. Stub; needs 2 to 5 screenshots or clips with one sentence each on what is wanted and what is not, for: how a layer stack reads on screen, how a unit changing height looks, how the layer ring and strip look, how a pulse looks.
228	
229	## Ways this could be wrong
230	
231	- Layer changes are instant in code today; a build that keeps the snap and ignores transition time passes a naive "layer changed" test.
232	- Visibility set changes but the fog render does not, or the render changes and the set does not.
233	- Cross-layer factors applied to the wrong axis (target's layer vs observer's).
234	- Vantage doubling applied to same-layer radius instead of cross-layer only.
235	- Pulse reveal persists after expiry, or cooldown resets on save and load.
236	- Preference and hard transfer both set but the wrong one wins.
237	- Blocked-layer path routes around on the wrong layer, or the unit auto-changes layer without an order.
238	- Ring colors read from the render's last-known layer instead of the delta.
239	- Cover blocks movement, or reduces damage, because a physics layer was reused.
240	- Layer count 5 in config with only 3 elevation bands, so layers 4 and 5 draw at layer 3's height.
241	
242	## Open ambiguity flags
243	
244	Q-E01-01, Q-001-01, Q-001-02, Q-001-03, Q-002-01, Q-002-02, Q-003-01, Q-004-01, Q-004-02, Q-005-01, Q-006-01, Q-006-02, Q-008-01, Q-009-01. Details in `docs/northstar/ambiguity_register.md`.
245	
246	## Depends on
247	
248	- E-11 Units (unit types, sensor radius, transition time per type).
249	- E-12 Fog and sensors (sensor radius, interference zones, elevation sensor bonus).
250	- E-13 Movement and pathing (routing around blocked layers).
251	- E-17 Map generation (accessibility mask, vantage nodes, cover placement).
252	- E-16 Camera and HUD (layer strip, rings, elevation on screen).

# E-01 — Layer System

## Definition-completeness gate (run 2026-09-10)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Every story has at least one Given/When/Then rule with concrete values | Yes, 11 stories, 34 rules. Rules that depend on an open flag cite it inline. |
| Every input listed with range and rejection behavior | Yes, see Inputs. Two rejection behaviors are open (Q-002-02, Q-003-01). |
| Every output listed with where it is observable | Yes, see Outputs. On-screen elevation is open (Q-E01-01). |
| Implied-but-unstated behavior turned into flags | 14 new flags raised, Q-001-01 through Q-009-01. |
| Every visible-surface story has a reference | **No — by design a Godot design phase, not a screenshot pull.** `references/E-01/notes.md` records the plan: basic single-layer movement ships first, then Claude builds several interactive layer-system options in Godot for Westley to choose between; the choice fills the references. Blocks S-009, S-010, S-006 until then. |
| "Obviously working" in 60 seconds named | Yes, see below. |

**Gate verdict: not passed.** Blocked on 15 open flags (Q-E01-01 plus 14 new) and on references. Stories are Spec'd, not Ready.

## Purpose

The layer system is the game's strategic defining characteristic. The battlefield is not a flat plane. It is a stack of three to five vertical layers, and a unit is always on exactly one of them. Terrain blocks layers at specific places, so a force can go over an obstacle on a high layer or around it on a low one. Vision across layers is worse than vision on your own layer, so a force on a layer you cannot see is a threat you do not know about. Changing layers costs time and leaves the unit briefly vulnerable.

The promise this keeps for the player (vision_v2 Q6): a smaller force that understands surrounds, high ground, and layers beats a larger force that does not. Every rule below exists to make that promise testable.

Era-agnostic: the engine knows "layers 1 and 2 are blocked here." The era pack decides whether that is an asteroid, a mountain, or a reef. Launch ships the Settled Reach with no per-unit-type layer restrictions.

## Obviously working in 60 seconds

Spawn a Raider and a Bastion on layer 3 next to a tall obstacle. Order both to layer 5. The Raider rises visibly within a second, the Bastion takes several seconds, and each unit's ring changes color when its layer changes. Place an enemy on layer 1 under the obstacle: neither unit sees it. Move an enemy onto layer 4 within half the Raider's sensor range: the Raider sees it, the Bastion does not until it is closer. Fire a pulse: the layer-1 enemy appears for two seconds, then vanishes. Order the Raider to layer 1 through the obstacle: it does not change layer until it moves clear of the blocked zone, then drops.

## Stories

### S-001 — The map decides where each layer is open
As a commander, I want terrain to block specific layers at specific places, so that going over, going around, and hiding in the blocked layers are real choices.

Rules
- R-001-01  Given a map position where layers 1 and 2 are blocked and layers 3 to 5 are open, When any unit on layer 1 or 2 is ordered to move through that position, Then its path avoids the blocked area on its current layer and the unit never occupies the blocked position on layers 1 or 2.
- R-001-02  Given the same position, When a unit on layer 3 moves through it, Then the unit passes straight through with no detour.
- R-001-03  Given a position where every layer is open, When any unit moves through it, Then no layer restriction applies.
- R-001-04  Given any map generated for any era pack, When the map is queried for layer accessibility at every sampled position and layer, Then the answer is a binary open or blocked per layer, and the count of layers is the same for every position on that map.

Inputs: map layer accessibility mask (binary per layer per position); unit position; unit current layer.
Outputs: unit path; unit position over time; layer accessibility query result.
Open flags: Q-001-01 (layer count per map), Q-001-02 (which end is layer 1), Q-001-03 (no route on current layer).

### S-002 — Hard layer transfer
As a commander, I want to order selected units to a specific layer, so that I can commit a force to a height when timing matters.

Rules
- R-002-01  Given a selected unit on layer 3 at a position where layer 5 is open, When the player issues a hard transfer to layer 5, Then the unit begins its transition on the same tick and finishes on layer 5 after its transition duration (S-004).
- R-002-02  Given a selected unit at a position where layer 5 is blocked, When the player issues a hard transfer to layer 5, Then the unit keeps executing its current orders on its current layer, and begins the transition on the first tick it occupies a position where layer 5 is open.
- R-002-03  Given a unit with a pending hard transfer, When the player issues a second hard transfer to a different layer, Then the first transfer is discarded and only the second is pending.
- R-002-04  Given a unit with a pending hard transfer, When the player issues a move order, Then the transfer stays pending; a move order never clears a transfer.
- R-002-05  Given a hard transfer to the unit's current layer, When it is issued, Then it is accepted and completes immediately with no transition and no vulnerability window.
- R-002-06  Given a hard transfer to a layer outside the map's layer range, When it is issued, Then it is rejected and the unit's state does not change.
- R-002-07  Given a hard transfer order for a mixed selection, When it is issued, Then every unit in the selection gets its own pending transfer and each resolves independently by its own position and duration.

Inputs: layer command (target layer, integer in map range); selection (1 to N units); unit position; accessibility mask.
Outputs: per-unit pending transfer; per-unit layer field in the tick delta; transition start and end events.
Open flags: Q-002-01 (non-adjacent target passes through intermediates or not), Q-002-02 (pending transfer never expires, or expires on arrival at the move destination).

### S-003 — Layer preference
As a commander, I want to give units a standing preference for a layer, so that a scouting group stays high and a siege group stays low without me re-ordering them at every obstacle.

Rules
- R-003-01  Given a selected unit with no preference, When the player sets preference to layer 2, Then the unit's preference is 2 and it begins a transition to layer 2 on the first tick it is at a position where layer 2 is open and it is not already on layer 2.
- R-003-02  Given a unit with preference 2 currently on layer 4 because layer 2 is blocked here, When the unit moves to a position where layer 2 is open, Then it begins its transition to layer 2 on that tick without a new order.
- R-003-03  Given a unit with preference 2 at a position where layer 2 is blocked, When any number of ticks pass, Then the unit continues its current orders on its current layer and never stalls or stops to wait.
- R-003-04  Given a unit with preference 2, When the player issues a hard transfer to layer 4, Then the preference is cleared and the hard transfer proceeds.
- R-003-05  Given a unit with preference 2, When the player issues the clear-preference action, Then the preference is cleared and the unit stays on its current layer.
- R-003-06  Given a unit with preference 2, When the player sets preference 3, Then the preference is 3 and any pending transition toward 2 is replaced.
- R-003-07  Given the modifier key held, When the player presses 1 through 5, Then that is a preference assignment, not a control-group recall; and Given the modifier key released, When the player presses 1 through 5, Then that is the standard control-group recall.
- R-003-08  Given a saved mission, When it is loaded, Then every unit's preference is restored exactly.

Inputs: preference command (layer integer or clear); modifier key state; selection.
Outputs: per-unit preferred layer in the tick delta; preference indicator on screen (S-009); save file.
Open flags: Q-003-01 (modifier key default and clear-preference input).

### S-004 — Changing layers takes time and leaves you exposed
As a commander, I want a layer change to cost time that depends on the unit type, so that hopping layers is a commitment and not a free dodge.

Rules
- R-004-01  Given a Raider ordered from layer 3 to layer 4 at an open position, When the transition starts, Then the unit is on layer 4 exactly one transition duration later, with the duration taken from the unit type's transition time [Q-004-01 for the confirmed numbers; current config: Raider 1.0 s, Interceptor 1.2 s, Vanguard 2.5 s, Warden 2.0 s, Bombard 4.0 s, Bastion 5.0 s].
- R-004-02  Given a unit mid-transition, When any unit on its old layer would otherwise attack it, Then the attack does not target it, and the transitioning unit itself cannot attack.
- R-004-03  Given two units of different types ordered to the same layer at the same tick, When the faster type completes, Then the slower type is still mid-transition, and completion order always matches transition-time order.
- R-004-04  Given a unit mid-transition, When a new hard transfer to another layer is issued, Then the unit completes the current transition first and the new transfer becomes pending.
- R-004-05  Given the same seed and the same command stream, When the mission runs twice, Then every transition starts and ends on the same tick both times.

Inputs: unit type transition time (per type, config); transition start tick.
Outputs: unit layer field; transitioning flag in the tick delta; attack eligibility.
Open flags: Q-004-01 (confirm durations), Q-004-02 (movement and new-layer targeting during the window).

### S-005 — Seeing across layers is worse than seeing on your own
As a commander, I want cross-layer vision to shrink with layer distance, so that a force on a layer I am not watching is a real threat.

Rules
- R-005-01  Given an observer with sensor radius 1,000 on layer 3 and an enemy on layer 3 at distance 900, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is in the observer's visible set.
- R-005-02  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 4 at distance 400, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is visible (adjacent layer factor 0.50, effective radius 500).
- R-005-03  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 4 at distance 600, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is not visible.
- R-005-04  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 5 at distance 150, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is visible (two-layer factor 0.20, effective radius 200); at distance 250 it is not.
- R-005-05  Given the same observer and an enemy on layer 1 (two layers below) or any layer three or more away, When one tick passes, Then the enemy is never visible by passive detection at any distance.
- R-005-06  Given an observer standing at a vantage node, When the same enemies are placed, Then the adjacent factor is 1.00, the two-layer factor is 0.40, and a three-layer enemy is visible at factor 0.20.
- R-005-07  Given an observer inside a sensor interference zone of intensity 0.5, When an enemy is on an adjacent layer, Then the effective cross-layer radius is sensor radius × 0.50 × 0.50.
- R-005-08  Given fog on, When an enemy on another layer is outside the effective cross-layer radius, Then it is hidden from the player exactly as a same-layer enemy outside sensor radius is hidden: no silhouette, no marker, no special treatment.

Inputs: observer layer, position, sensor radius; target layer, position; vantage membership; interference intensity at observer position.
Outputs: per-unit visible set in the tick delta; player-visible unit list; fog reveal on screen.
Open flags: Q-005-01 (what counts as standing at a vantage node).

### S-006 — Sensor pulse
As a commander, I want to spend a pulse to see every layer around a unit for a moment, so that scouting before a commitment is a decision with a cost.

Rules
- R-006-01  Given a pulse-capable unit with its pulse ready, When the player triggers the pulse, Then every enemy on every layer within the pulse radius is in the player's visible set for the next 2.0 seconds of sim time (40 ticks at 20 ticks per second).
- R-006-02  Given a pulse that started 2.0 seconds ago, When the next tick runs, Then enemies revealed only by the pulse leave the visible set.
- R-006-03  Given a pulse fired on tick T, When the player tries again before tick T plus 20.0 seconds (400 ticks), Then the command is rejected and the cooldown is unchanged.
- R-006-04  Given the pulse-capable unit is inside an interference zone of intensity 0.5, When it pulses, Then the pulse radius is halved.
- R-006-05  Given a pulse reveals an enemy on layer 1 while the observer is on layer 5, When the pulse expires and no passive detection applies, Then the enemy is hidden again.

Inputs: pulse command; pulse-capable unit; pulse radius (config); cooldown state.
Outputs: pulse active flag and remaining cooldown in the tick delta; revealed set; cooldown ring on the HUD; visible pulse effect on screen.
Open flags: Q-006-01 (which units pulse, radius, and whether the pulse is the unit's one ability), Q-006-02 (last-seen markers after expiry).

### S-007 — Cover blocks sight by height
As a commander, I want a tall obstacle to hide units on more layers than a short one, so that where I put a force relative to terrain changes what the enemy can see.

Rules
- R-007-01  Given an obstacle whose height reaches layer 2 between an observer and a target both on layer 1, When one tick passes, Then the target is not visible.
- R-007-02  Given the same obstacle and both units on layer 3, When one tick passes, Then the target is visible (the obstacle does not reach layer 3).
- R-007-03  Given a target hidden behind cover, When it attacks an observer that cannot see it, Then the attack lands and the target stays hidden; firing never reveals.
- R-007-04  Given a target visible despite nearby cover, When it takes damage, Then damage is unmodified; cover is never a damage reduction.
- R-007-05  Given cover in a unit's path, When it moves, Then movement is unaffected; cover never blocks movement.

Inputs: obstacle position, radius, height; observer and target positions and layers.
Outputs: visible set; damage applied; unit path.
Open flags: none beyond Q-001-01 (obstacle height thresholds depend on the layer count and spacing).

### S-008 — Combat across layers
As a commander, I want to know whether a unit can shoot at an enemy one layer above it, so that layer position is a positional decision and not a guess.

Rules
- R-008-01  Given an attacker on layer 3 and a visible enemy on layer 3 in range, When the attacker is idle or attack-moving, Then it engages.
- R-008-02  Given an attacker on layer 3 and a visible enemy on layer 4 in range, When the attacker is idle or attack-moving, Then [Q-008-01 decides: it does not engage (current code), or it engages with a stated range or damage modifier].
- R-008-03  Given a Bombard's area attack centered on layer 3, When enemies stand on layers 2 and 4 inside the radius, Then [Q-008-01 decides whether they take damage].

Inputs: attacker layer, target layer, range, visibility.
Outputs: attack events; HP changes in the tick delta.
Open flags: Q-008-01 (prototype: same-layer only), Q-008-02 (the cross-layer damage and vision design and its research program; the game's most important undefined mechanic).

### S-009 — I can see what layer every unit is on
As a commander, I want to see at a glance which layer each unit is on and which layer I am focused on, so that I never have to guess who can see whom.

Rules
- R-009-01  Given any unit on screen, When the player looks at it, Then a ring under the unit shows one color per layer, and the color changes on the tick the unit's layer changes.
- R-009-02  Given a unit toggled toward another layer, When the player looks at it, Then the target disc on its spindle (R-009-05) gains an outline and a chevron, a waypoint-like mark of where it is going, distinct from the lit current-layer disc.
- R-009-05  Given any unit on screen, When drawn, Then a thin rod beside it carries five small discs, one per layer, the unit's own disc lit at about 50 percent, adjacent discs at 10 to 20 percent, discs two away at 5 percent (the Floor Spindle); and its grid tiers are flat discs that tilt to the ground's slope at each layer's height (Terrace Reading). Both are subdued, never loud, and never block the view of the battlefield behind them.
- R-009-06  Given units hidden from the player by the current perspective (behind terrain or another layer's ground), When the player looks at the scene, Then something tells them they are not seeing the whole picture [Q-009-02: the mechanism, such as a small mark on the occluding units].
- R-009-03  Given the layer strip on the HUD, When the player clicks a layer or presses Tab, Then the focused layer changes and the strip highlights the new one.
- R-009-04  Given the same selection and camera, When a T2 screenshot is taken, Then the ring colors match the sim's per-unit layer field for every unit in view.

Inputs: unit layer, preferred layer; focus click or Tab.
Outputs: ring color per unit; spindle and terrace discs; target mark; focused layer on the strip.
Open flags: Q-009-02 (the occlusion indicator). Q-009-01 is closed: focus is purely visual, other layers dim slightly. Look chosen through the options pass, `docs/northstar/research/options/layer-system/`, Q-E01-08; Godot renders of it fill `references/E-01/notes.md`.

### S-010 — Layers read as height on screen
As a commander, I want a unit on a higher layer to sit visibly higher than one on a lower layer, so that the layer stack reads as a stack and not as a color code.

Rules
- R-010-01  Given a unit on layer L at position (x, y), When it is drawn, Then its world-space height is the layer's elevation from the map's layer mapping [Q-E01-01 decides where the mapping lives; current code: three z-bands 0 to 30, 30 to 100, 100 to 300 for a five-layer count, which is itself a defect].
- R-010-02  Given a unit transitioning from layer 3 to 4, When frames render during the transition, Then its drawn height moves from layer 3's elevation to layer 4's over the transition duration, not as a snap.
- R-010-03  Given a fixed camera and a unit ordered up one layer, When a T2 screenshot is taken before and after, Then the unit's screen position differs vertically by more than 5 percent of the viewport height.

Inputs: layer to elevation mapping; camera.
Outputs: unit world position on screen.
Open flags: Q-E01-01. Reference required: `references/E-01/notes.md`, missing.

### S-011 — Era packs may restrict unit types to layers
As an era designer, I want an era pack to say which layers a unit type may occupy, so that a submarine era or a ground-only era works on the same engine without code changes.

Rules
- R-011-01  Given the Settled Reach era pack (no restriction mask), When any unit type is ordered to any open layer, Then it is accepted.
- R-011-02  Given an era pack whose mask permits type X on layers 4 and 5 only, When a type-X unit is ordered to layer 2, Then the order is rejected and the unit stays on its layer.
- R-011-03  Given the same pack, When a type-X unit spawns, Then it spawns on a permitted layer.
- R-011-04  Given the same pack, When a type-X unit has preference 2, Then the preference is rejected at assignment time.

Inputs: era pack restriction mask (per unit type, set of layers; absent means unrestricted).
Outputs: command acceptance; spawn layer.
Open flags: none. Launch scope: capability present, mask absent (A-294, A-321).

## Inputs

| Input | Source | Range | Rejection |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layer accessibility mask | Map generator | Binary per layer per sampled position | Not player-issued |
| Layer count | Map or engine | 3 to 5 [Q-001-01] | Map generation fails outside range |
| Hard transfer | Player | Target layer in map range, selection 1 to N | Out of range: rejected, no state change. Era mask forbids: rejected |
| Preference set | Player | Layer in map range or clear | Same as hard transfer |
| Modifier key | Player | Held or released | None |
| Pulse | Player | Pulse-capable selected unit, cooldown ready | On cooldown or not capable: rejected |
| Unit type transition time | Config | 1.0 to 5.0 s [Q-004-01] | Not player-issued |
| Sensor radius, vantage membership, interference intensity | Sim | Per unit, per position | Not player-issued |
| Era restriction mask | Era pack | Per unit type, subset of layers, or absent | Malformed pack fails to load |

## Outputs

| Output | Observable where |
|---|---|
| Unit layer | Tick delta unit entry; ring color on screen; save file |
| Preferred layer | Tick delta unit entry; preference indicator; save file |
| Transitioning flag and remaining time | Tick delta unit entry; drawn height mid-tween |
| Visible set per unit; player-visible list | Tick delta; fog reveal on screen |
| Pulse active, cooldown remaining | Tick delta; HUD cooldown ring; pulse effect on screen |
| Command rejections | Command acknowledgement in the tick delta with a reason code |
| Focused layer | HUD strip highlight |

## Invariants

- A unit is on exactly one layer at every tick, including mid-transition (it is on its old layer until the transition completes).
- No unit ever occupies a position and layer the mask marks blocked.
- Visible set is symmetric in rule, not in outcome: A sees B does not imply B sees A.
- Same seed and command stream produce identical layer, visibility, and transition traces.
- Cover never changes damage or movement.

## Scale requirements

Numbers to be confirmed by Westley in Stage 3. Proposed: 1,000 units computing cross-layer visibility against 1,000 units in under 2 ms per tick; 10,000 units in under 20 ms per tick; accessibility queries at 10,000 per tick in under 1 ms.

## Look and behavior references

`references/E-01/notes.md`. Stub; needs 2 to 5 screenshots or clips with one sentence each on what is wanted and what is not, for: how a layer stack reads on screen, how a unit changing height looks, how the layer ring and strip look, how a pulse looks.

## Ways this could be wrong

- Layer changes are instant in code today; a build that keeps the snap and ignores transition time passes a naive "layer changed" test.
- Visibility set changes but the fog render does not, or the render changes and the set does not.
- Cross-layer factors applied to the wrong axis (target's layer vs observer's).
- Vantage doubling applied to same-layer radius instead of cross-layer only.
- Pulse reveal persists after expiry, or cooldown resets on save and load.
- Preference and hard transfer both set but the wrong one wins.
- Blocked-layer path routes around on the wrong layer, or the unit auto-changes layer without an order.
- Ring colors read from the render's last-known layer instead of the delta.
- Cover blocks movement, or reduces damage, because a physics layer was reused.
- Layer count 5 in config with only 3 elevation bands, so layers 4 and 5 draw at layer 3's height.

## Open ambiguity flags

Q-E01-01, Q-001-01, Q-001-02, Q-001-03, Q-002-01, Q-002-02, Q-003-01, Q-004-01, Q-004-02, Q-005-01, Q-006-01, Q-006-02, Q-008-01, Q-009-01. Details in `docs/northstar/ambiguity_register.md`.

## Depends on

- E-11 Units (unit types, sensor radius, transition time per type).
- E-12 Fog and sensors (sensor radius, interference zones, elevation sensor bonus).
- E-13 Movement and pathing (routing around blocked layers).
- E-17 Map generation (accessibility mask, vantage nodes, cover placement).
- E-16 Camera and HUD (layer strip, rings, elevation on screen).

## Q-E01-02 [closed] Layer System
Q: When a unit's layer changes, does it visibly move to the new elevation, and over how many ticks?
A: (b), confirmed. `bible_combat.md` A-354: a unit transitioning between layers spends a per-unit-type duration (Strike fastest, Siege slowest) unable to attack or be targeted by units on its old layer — a real vulnerability window, not an instant snap or an unrestricted tween. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-03 [closed] Layer System
Q: What can a unit on layer 2 see on layers 1 and 3, and at what range compared to its own layer?
A: (c), confirmed with the concrete numbers. `bible_world.md` A-432: passive cross-layer cone detection degrades by distance — adjacent layer ×0.50, two layers away ×0.20, three+ layers away no passive detection at all; vantage nodes double these factors and extend one layer further. A-433 adds an active sensor pulse (reveal all layers in a radius for ~2s, ~20s cooldown) on top of the passive cone. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-04 [closed] Layer System
Q: Do layers change pathing, damage, or cover? Which of the three, and how?
A: Nuanced answer, none of the three literally as posed. Layers affect **pathing** (`bible_world.md`'s `layer_accessibility_mask` blocks movement per layer/position) and **vision** (the cone/pulse model above), and indirectly **cover** (an obstacle's height determines which layers it blocks line of sight on, per `bible_combat.md` A-337 / `bible_world.md` A-388's `LAYER_Z_FLOORS` rule). Layers do **not** directly affect damage — that's a separate `elevation` gradient gated by `ELEVATION_DAMAGE_BONUS_ENABLED`, disabled for the space era at launch (`bible_world.md` A-435, `bible_combat.md` A-338). Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-05 [closed] Layer System
Q: What does the player see in the HUD about a selected unit's layer and about enemies on other layers?
A: (b), confirmed. `bible_combat.md` A-312: a layer-selector strip lets the player switch which layer has their focus. A-299 (deferred pending visual-mechanism research): a per-unit layer-preference indicator; A-313: a layer-color ring under every unit shows current layer at a glance. No dedicated "enemies on other layers" HUD readout beyond the fog/sensor system itself. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-06 [closed] Layer System
Q: Under fog, how does an enemy on another layer appear compared to one on the same layer?
A: (a), mechanism-wise. There's no special silhouette treatment for a different-layer enemy — it's the same hidden/revealed binary as same-layer fog, just evaluated against a shorter (cone-degraded, per Q-E01-03) or reset-to-hidden (pulse-expired, per `bible_world.md` A-433) effective sensor range. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-07 [closed] Layer System
Q: Is the layer system still "the" strategic defining characteristic, and if so what is the one-sentence player-facing promise it must keep?
A: Yes, still the defining characteristic. Promise: a player with an inferior force but understanding of positional tactics (surround, high ground, game-theory positioning) can overcome the opposition — the layer system, high skill ceiling, specific unit knowledge decide outcomes over raw force. Answered live in Stage 1 vision interview, `vision_v2.md` Q6, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-08 [closed] E-01 / S-009, S-010, S-006
Q: References missing. Needed: 2 to 5 screenshots or clips showing how a layer stack should read on screen, how a unit changing height should look, how the layer ring and strip should look, how a pulse should look; one sentence each on the target and one on what is not wanted.
A: Resolved by the options pass instead of screenshots. Answered by Westley, 2026-09-23, verbatim: "For layer system I'd like to combine Terrace Reading with Floor Spindle and have both display, but the neither should be visually loud, just a subdued indicator (not blocking the view). We'll need to come up with a method to indicate to the player that there are units blocked by their current perspective, like a little exlamation point on the blocking units, this is to be determined and open, but I think it'd be good game design for us to indiciate to the user that they're not seeing the whole picture in some fashion." Folded into E-01 R-009-02, R-009-05, R-009-06; the occlusion indicator is Q-009-02.

## Q-001-01 [closed] E-01 / S-001
Q: How many layers does a map have? `bible_combat.md` says 3 to 5 per map; code has `LAYER_COUNT = 5` but only three elevation bands (`LAYER_Z_FLOORS`). Is the count fixed engine-wide with maps blocking unused layers, or variable per map?
A: (a), confirmed by Q-E01-01 verdict: always 5 layers engine-wide. Settled Reach does not restrict any layers; all 5 are open at every position. Map generator does not vary layer count per map; the 3-to-5 bible language is stale. Answered by Westley, 2026-09-12.

## Q-002-02 [closed] E-01 / S-002
Q: A hard transfer is pending because the target layer is blocked here. How long does it stay pending?
A: (b), "until move order completes." Answered by Westley, 2026-09-13.

## Q-003-01 [closed] E-01 / S-003
Q: The preference modifier key default and the clear-preference input are both "TBD" in the bible. What are they?
A: (a), modifier Alt + 1..5 for layer preference, Alt + 0 to clear. Answered by Westley, 2026-09-16.

Note Warden (Line) is faster than Vanguard (Line), which the "Strike fastest, Siege slowest" rule allows but does not explain.

A: (b), confirmed. `bible_combat.md` A-354: a unit transitioning between layers spends a per-unit-type duration (Strike fastest, Siege slowest) unable to attack or be targeted by units on its old layer — a real vulnerability window, not an instant snap or an unrestricted tween. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-03 [closed] Layer System
Q: What can a unit on layer 2 see on layers 1 and 3, and at what range compared to its own layer?
A: (c), confirmed with the concrete numbers. `bible_world.md` A-432: passive cross-layer cone detection degrades by distance — adjacent layer ×0.50, two layers away ×0.20, three+ layers away no passive detection at all; vantage nodes double these factors and extend one layer further. A-433 adds an active sensor pulse (reveal all layers in a radius for ~2s, ~20s cooldown) on top of the passive cone. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-04 [closed] Layer System
Q: Do layers change pathing, damage, or cover? Which of the three, and how?
A: Nuanced answer, none of the three literally as posed. Layers affect **pathing** (`bible_world.md`'s `layer_accessibility_mask` blocks movement per layer/position) and **vision** (the cone/pulse model above), and indirectly **cover** (an obstacle's height determines which layers it blocks line of sight on, per `bible_combat.md` A-337 / `bible_world.md` A-388's `LAYER_Z_FLOORS` rule). Layers do **not** directly affect damage — that's a separate `elevation` gradient gated by `ELEVATION_DAMAGE_BONUS_ENABLED`, disabled for the space era at launch (`bible_world.md` A-435, `bible_combat.md` A-338). Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-05 [closed] Layer System
Q: What does the player see in the HUD about a selected unit's layer and about enemies on other layers?
A: (b), confirmed. `bible_combat.md` A-312: a layer-selector strip lets the player switch which layer has their focus. A-299 (deferred pending visual-mechanism research): a per-unit layer-preference indicator; A-313: a layer-color ring under every unit shows current layer at a glance. No dedicated "enemies on other layers" HUD readout beyond the fog/sensor system itself. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

## Q-E01-06 [closed] Layer System
Q: Under fog, how does an enemy on another layer appear compared to one on the same layer?
A: (a), mechanism-wise. There's no special silhouette treatment for a different-layer enemy — it's the same hidden/revealed binary as same-layer fog, just evaluated against a shorter (cone-degraded, per Q-E01-03) or reset-to-hidden (pulse-expired, per `bible_world.md` A-433) effective sensor range. Closed from the Stage 1 audit, 2026-09-10.

Q: Is the layer system still "the" strategic defining characteristic, and if so what is the one-sentence player-facing promise it must keep?
A: Yes, still the defining characteristic. Promise: a player with an inferior force but understanding of positional tactics (surround, high ground, game-theory positioning) can overcome the opposition — the layer system, high skill ceiling, specific unit knowledge decide outcomes over raw force. ## 10. Decision (2026-09-23)

=== map-view decision
## 10. Decision (2026-09-23)

Westley, verbatim: "For the zoom band, I really like the sand table idea, but I'd like to see a prototype before I commit to it. This is the sort of thing that's really hard to pull off, but I'd really like to see something like the sand table from Dune, the execution would have to be really good on this, we'd need to make a prototype that's low resolution (large blocks to represent height), and design it such that the resolution (size of the grains of sand, and hence detail) could be turned up and down. Obviously once it gets really fine grained, the detail will be immense but so will the graphics load. It'd also be nice if the users had a 45 degree angle option of the same map, with layers seperated enough for specific sets of units to be visible. This is worth significant protytping and tuning, this is a complex mechanism. I'd like to brainstorm additional options for indicating which layer specific units and unit groups are one, because the pin option is a good option but I don't think it has to be the only one. Mark further research needed."

Recorded as: Sand Table is the candidate, prototype before commitment (block-resolution table with a grain-size dial, plus a 45° view with layers separated); more layer-mark ideas beyond pins wanted (Q-103-05, Q-103-06; E-16 S-161).
=== control-groups decision
## 10. Decision (2026-09-23)

Westley, verbatim: "For control group depth, I want to combine Recall and Narrow with The Comb, recall can be the default for control groups and multi-layer movement, and comb can be the way to move individual layers within a group."

Recorded as: Recall and Narrow as the default for groups and multi-layer movement, the Comb for moving individual layers within a group (Q-105-02).
=== unit-traits decision
## 10. Decision (2026-09-23)

Westley, verbatim: "For passive traits, I'd kinda like them to be unlockable, like Dead by Daylight or Age of Empires 3. However, traits and abilities are never more powerful than a player's positioning ability, this is a core rule for the game: a player with "weak" abilities/traits that understands strategy and the layer system better will trump any player with "strong" abilities/traits that doesn't. Layer system damage is weighted much more heavily than abilities/passives, and we'll minimize traits/abilities that are unlockable that give players an "edge" in terms of vision across layers. This one is pretty decided (we'll make the cards cool so the players have a desire to unlock them), no need for a second pass on this decision."

Recorded as: Unlockable trait cards (Dead by Daylight, Age of Empires 3 register) under a core rule: cards and abilities never outrank positioning, layer damage weighs more, cross-layer-vision cards minimized. Decided, no second pass (Q-083-02, Q-083-03).
=== difficulty-knobs decision
## 10. Decision (2026-09-23)

Westley, verbatim: "For enemy macro, I don't like either of those. I think that there are two places that we need to scale the AI's ability: economic prosperity (more resources), and multi-layer intelligence. I had an idea that I want you to record as a desired piece of the layer system: players can invest (though costly) in units that give them better vision, a unit like the units in Starcraft that were invisible, but could see. The intelligent player gets one but has a slightly smaller army, but wins the fight because they knew where the opponents army was and created an intelligent surround with units on specific layers organized so that the opponent couldn't see it until it was too late. This is something the AI's should strive for when they're on hard mode, positional awareness and awareness of what combination of units would need to be on what layers in order to trump the other player's units given what layers those units are on."

Recorded as: Neither. Difficulty scales the enemy's economic prosperity and its multi-layer intelligence; a costly seer unit is a desired piece of the layer system (Q-125-02, Q-125-03, Q-E12-01).

## Option A — The Angle Rack

Five fixed vantage angles — top-down, 45° overhead, horizontal, 45° upward, a single unit's shoulder — hopped between at will. Pan, zoom, and edge-scroll work as in classic view; only the angle is chosen from a memorized set, like a keyboard shortcut.
## Option B — The Anchor Ring

One continuous crane in place of fixed angles: hold a key and drag anywhere from overhead to eye level, at any distance the height floor allows, and drop personal bookmarks worth returning to.
## Option C — Layer Peel (wild)

The five layers separate like a fanned hand of cards around your focus point. A threat two layers from where you're looking is no longer hidden behind height — it sits on its own card, beside you.
## Option D — Ghost Walk (wild)

An intangible eye released into the fight at human height. It has no body, cannot act or be targeted, and cannot ride or become a unit — it only watches — but climbs or drops between layers exactly as a transitioning unit would, so the layer gap you order units to cross is one you can feel.
## Option A — Recall and Narrow

Nothing new to learn. Bind each army as any control group: select, Ctrl plus a digit. The group holds whatever mix of layers it had at bind time, and the digit recalls all of it regardless of layer. To work one layer, recall the group, then tap that layer's hotkey; the selection narrows, and the strip's focus never moves because of it. A group is a group, a narrow is a narrow, and the two compose.
## Option B — Layer Sub-Tabs

The top-level bind is unchanged. The instant a bound group holds units on more than one layer, its tab grows a second row: one chip per layer present, ring color and live count. A player reaches one slice by holding the digit and tapping the layer number while held — one chord, not two taps — or clicking the chip. The bare digit still recalls the whole army.
## Option C — The Comb (wild)

No cycling, no chord. Holding a digit still recalls the whole army. While held, the layer strip blooms: every layer that army occupies lights up as a bar sized to its unit count there. Dragging across one, two, or three bars and releasing makes those layers the live selection; the rest drops out, and letting go collapses the strip to five thin rings. One gesture, hold-drag-release, picks any layer combination without a second key.

Westley, 2026-09-23, verbatim: "the layer system dynamics are not fully defined, just an idea at this point. How units interact with each other cross-layer in terms of damage and vision are not yet defined, and that's probably the most important/unique part of this game. Let's make hashing that out a priority, I believe that prototypes are in order, comprehensive analysis of what configuration of damage/vision/landscape would induce the highest skill ceiling. Maybe we could take the "surround" idea into 3D, and define our own "Art of War" for 3 dimensional battles. Let's draw from high altitude ariel battle research. This section of the game deserves some real thought and experimentation, but I don't know how to test it without humans in the loop. We'd have to map out with research what makes games of the past have a high skill ceiling." 
| CANDIDATES: (a) a Track R research program (research queue Q76): what gave past games a high skill ceiling, aerial and high-altitude combat doctrine, a 3D surround theory, then prototypes with humans in the loop [recommended]; (b) design by analysis alone; (c) other

This is something the AI's should strive for when they're on hard mode, positional awareness and awareness of what combination of units would need to be on what layers in order to trump the other player's units given what layers those units are on." Which unit, at what cost, and how it is countered? 
| CANDIDATES: (a) a roster role, a costly seer with wide cross-layer vision and no attack, visible only to other seers [recommended]; (b) an ability on an existing type; (c) decided with Q-008-02

## Option A — The Angle Rack

Five fixed vantage angles — top-down, 45° overhead, horizontal, 45° upward, a single unit's shoulder — hopped between at will. Pan, zoom, and edge-scroll work as in classic view; only the angle is chosen from a memorized set, like a keyboard shortcut.
## Option B — The Anchor Ring

One continuous crane in place of fixed angles: hold a key and drag anywhere from overhead to eye level, at any distance the height floor allows, and drop personal bookmarks worth returning to.
## Option C — Layer Peel (wild)

The five layers separate like a fanned hand of cards around your focus point. A threat two layers from where you're looking is no longer hidden behind height — it sits on its own card, beside you.
## Option D — Ghost Walk (wild)

An intangible eye released into the fight at human height. It has no body, cannot act or be targeted, and cannot ride or become a unit — it only watches — but climbs or drops between layers exactly as a transitioning unit would, so the layer gap you order units to cross is one you can feel.
## Option A — Recall and Narrow

Nothing new to learn. Bind each army as any control group: select, Ctrl plus a digit. The group holds whatever mix of layers it had at bind time, and the digit recalls all of it regardless of layer. To work one layer, recall the group, then tap that layer's hotkey; the selection narrows, and the strip's focus never moves because of it. A group is a group, a narrow is a narrow, and the two compose.
## Option B — Layer Sub-Tabs

The top-level bind is unchanged. The instant a bound group holds units on more than one layer, its tab grows a second row: one chip per layer present, ring color and live count. A player reaches one slice by holding the digit and tapping the layer number while held — one chord, not two taps — or clicking the chip. The bare digit still recalls the whole army.
## Option C — The Comb (wild)

No cycling, no chord. Holding a digit still recalls the whole army. While held, the layer strip blooms: every layer that army occupies lights up as a bar sized to its unit count there. Dragging across one, two, or three bars and releasing makes those layers the live selection; the rest drops out, and letting go collapses the strip to five thin rings. One gesture, hold-drag-release, picks any layer combination without a second key.

# E-01 Layer System — Look and behavior references

**Not external screenshots — a design phase.** The layer system is Ouroboros's most important, distinctive mechanic and is hard to change once built, so it earns a serious design phase instead of a reference pull from other games. Westley does not yet know exactly what it should look like; he will decide by interacting with real options.

## The plan (Westley, 2026-09-13)

1. **Build basic unit movement on a single layer first.** The earliest epics ship a plain one-layer movement prototype in Godot — no layer mechanic yet. This exists specifically to be the sandbox for step 2.
2. **Claude develops a plan to build several layer-system options in Godot** on top of that prototype — different looks and interactions for the stack, height changes, the layer ring/strip, and pulses — that Westley can play with and choose between.
3. Westley picks; the chosen option becomes the E-01 visual end-state and these references are filled with Godot renders of it.

Step 3 happened on paper: the options pass (`docs/northstar/research/options/layer-system/`) put four looks in front of Westley and on 2026-09-23 he chose Terrace Reading combined with Floor Spindle, both subdued (E-01 R-009-05), with a waypoint-like target mark (R-009-02) and an occlusion indicator still open (Q-009-02). Q-E01-08 is closed; the slots below are filled with Godot renders of that look as they are built.

## Westley's recorded layer ideas

Westley's layer decisions from this planning round are captured as closed rows in `docs/northstar/ambiguity_register.md` (Q-001-xx, Q-002-xx, Q-008-01): always 5 layers engine-wide; layer 1 is the bottom; no auto layer-change (the player owns it); one transition of 1–2 s regardless of distance; cross-layer combat is an intended strategic tuning lever (range/damage vary by layer offset), still under research. The Godot options in step 2 must honor these.

## Slots to fill once the Godot options exist

|---|---|---|---|---|

| 02 | S-002, S-004 | Unit changing height (clip) | the 1–2 s transition reads as a height change | — |
| 03 | S-009 | Layer-color ring under a unit + HUD layer strip | current layer legible per-unit and globally | — |
| 04 | S-006 | Sensor pulse reveal and fade (clip) | the reveal sweep and its decay | — |

content.text:
I found the artifact: the **Options Atlas** (https://claude.ai/artifact/6571aySFhmoQ1i4XswDhNm). It covers 11 features, not 9, and it was last updated 2026-09-22, before your decisions. The repo copy in `docs/northstar/research/options/` is the current one, because your 2026-09-23 decisions are recorded there. I read the layer-system pieces from the repo, plus the camera, map-view, control-groups, unit-traits and difficulty decisions that touch layers, then E-01 and the register.

## Decided

**Mechanics (from the Stage 1 audit and your answers):**
- There are always 5 layers in every era, and layer 1 is the bottom. In land eras without flight, the upper layers are still land, such as mountains.
- Terrain blocks layers at specific places, and units route around blocked areas. The player owns the layer, so nothing ever changes it automatically.
- A layer change is one tween of 1 to 2 seconds. Per-type durations: Raider 1.0, Interceptor 1.2, Warden 2.0, Vanguard 2.5, Bombard 4.0, Bastion 5.0.
  - The unit can be attacked from its old layer until the halfway point, and the new layer can hit it after halfway.
- Passive cross-layer vision is ×0.50 one layer away and ×0.20 two layers away. It is none at three or more.
- The sensor pulse reveals all layers for 2 seconds, with a 20-second cooldown and a 10-second ghost marker afterward.
  - For now it belongs to the Interceptor, "for now".
- Fog is a plain hidden or revealed state, with no special silhouette for other layers.
- Obstacle height decides which layers a cover blocks for sight. Cover never reduces damage or blocks movement.
- Preference is Alt+1 to 5, and Alt+0 clears it. A hard transfer stays pending until the move order completes.
- For the prototype, combat is same-layer only (Q-008-01).

**Look and feel (options pass, 2026-09-23):**
- **Terrace Reading plus Floor Spindle**, both displayed, both subdued and never blocking the view.
  - Terrace Reading: each unit's grid tiers are flat discs that tilt to the slope at each layer's height.
  - Floor Spindle: a thin rod beside the unit carries 5 discs. Own layer about 50%, adjacent 10 to 20%, two away 5%.
- A waypoint-like mark on the target disc (outline plus chevron) shows where a unit is going.
- Colored ring under each unit, a layer strip on the right edge, and other layers dimmed slightly under focus.
- Vertical spacing is per era (large in space, small on land) and sets no fixed numbers.
- Camera: **Angle Rack and Layer Peel both**, with Layer Peel optional, plus a key that flips the view 180°.
- Control groups: **Recall and Narrow** as the default, and **the Comb** for moving individual layers within a group.
- Trait cards are unlockable but never outrank positioning. Layer damage weighs more than any ability, and cross-layer-vision cards are minimized.
- Difficulty scales the enemy's economic prosperity and its "multi-layer intelligence".

## Not defined

**The core (your words: "the most important/unique part of this game"):**
1. **Cross-layer damage and vision (Q-008-02).**
   - Nothing is defined beyond the prototype's same-layer-only rule.
   - The question is what range and damage apply across layers, and how a 3D surround works.
   - Research item Q76 is open. It calls for a brief and then prototypes with humans in the loop, and its brief has not been written yet.
   - E-01's notes still call cross-layer combat "an intended strategic tuning lever".
   - Q-E01-04 says layers never affect damage directly, but a separate elevation damage bonus exists in code and is disabled for the launch era. Those two may conflict with whatever Q-008-02 decides.
2. **The seer unit (Q-E12-01).**
   - You want a costly unit with better vision, like StarCraft's invisible-but-seeing units.
   - Its role, cost and counter are all open.
   - How it relates to the Interceptor's pulse is also open, since both give cross-layer sight.
3. **How layers relate to terrain height.**
   - Terrace Reading implies layers are terraces of the terrain. The brief's question of whether a layer is a terrace or a free altitude band was not answered.
   - R-010-01 still calls the old three-band mapping a defect, and no rule states the per-era spacing.
   - How units reach the upper layers in a land era is also unstated.

**Needs design work:**
- **Occlusion indicator (Q-009-02).** How the player is told that hidden units exist. Your sketch was an exclamation mark on the occluding units.
- **Camera controls (Q-103-04).** Keys, presets, the flip's rotation center, and whether the peel's focus and the strip's focus are one control.
- **Map view (Q-103-05, Q-103-06).**
  - The Sand Table is a candidate pending a prototype.
  - Layer marks on that view are open, and pins are one option you don't want to be the only one.
- **Enemy multi-layer intelligence (Q-125-03).** What hard mode strives for, and how the AI chooses which units go on which layers.
- **Trait unlock and weighting test (Q-083-03).** How "positioning outweighs any card" is checked in tuning.
- **Vantage nodes (Q-005-01).** Pinned off for the prototype. R-005-06 still contains the vantage numbers as if they were live.

**Bible hygiene in E-01:**
- The purpose line and the layer-count input row still say "3 to 5" layers.
- The gate verdict says 15 open flags, but most are closed.
- No reference renders exist yet for the chosen look.

## Built so far

- **Sim:** the per-type transition times and the cross-layer vision factors are real in `fog.c`. Attacks are same-layer only in `unit.c`. The map layer-mask functions look like unwired stubs, but I didn't read them closely.
- **Tests:** `tests/csim` has no E-01 test files, so none of E-01's rules have fenced tests yet.
- **Client:** the live tactical view has no layer rendering that I could find.
- **Prototype:** a two-layer prototype exists at `scenes/mockups/layers/`. It has a toy sim, a 60° camera and a QA checklist.

## Where I'd start

Q-008-02 gates everything else. The occlusion indicator, the seer unit, AI difficulty, vertical spacing and the map-view marks all depend on what cross-layer damage and vision actually do.

**My lean (opinion, not a decision):** start by defining the design space for Q-008-02 together, before any research agents or prototypes. That means naming the axes (range versus layer offset, damage versus offset, vision asymmetry, what blocks fire), sketching 3 or 4 candidate models, and asking of each what a "smaller force wins by surround in 3D" looks like. That gives Q76's research brief and prototype plan something concrete to test.

Do you want to start there, or take a smaller item first (for example the terrace-versus-altitude question, which unblocks the vertical spacing rules)?

"The player owns the layer, so nothing ever changes it automatically." Unless their units are forced because of terrain. 
  If they move-command someplace that doesn't have access to the layer they're on, but does have access on another layer 
  that they can transition to, then their units automatically transition (like units walking up a mountain). Record that 
  decision. - I'd like to start ( idea about layer simulation, simple prototype to tune numbers to produce strategy 
  situations ) a specific method of figuring out how we'll do this. We will build a "toy" prototype. It will have the basic
  functions of the game, and be very fast, all C, bare minimum visuals maybe with python game library or something simple. 
  It will contain the restraints of the system, layers, damage, vision, landscape. The prototype will run "simulations" of 
  unit complex combinations: position, orientation, damage, health, anything that we can vary in an RTS. We'll use this 
  simulator to document the relationships between all the variables and find the places that the "lines cross". We'll use 
  this as a map for tuning units across different eras, and maintaining strategic depth. For example, we may notice that 
  changing the vision variable only produces only strategic depth at a specific "value" given the values of all the other 
  variables, however, if we change another one, the "lines cross"
</pasted_content id="bf70">

 in more than one place, and induce strategic depth from two configurations of variables instead of one. This will require significant iterations and tuning, so the algorithms need to be fast. This is just an idea in my head currently, I want to explore it further and verify it works with a simple prototype before we commit to building the full thing. - We'll need to clearly define what "strategic depth" looks like, but we can grab from other similar high skill games like Starcraft 2. For example, in starcraft 2 when units have a layer advantage, they can shoot without being shot back. When units have a surround, the units in the concave with the surround win. Organizing your units in specific patterns can lead to better engagements, depending on the unit, it's vulnerabilities and abilities, etc. For example: templar are very weak and slow and expensive, but when they use storm they're devestating to low-health units. A player that effectively protects them has a higher chance of winning. We will need to map all these dimensions out before we build anything. Develop a plan to document the idea in the bible (with a pass after it's documented cross-referencing my original prompt with what was actually written for missed information or hallucinations),  map out the dimensions, build a toy prototype of it, and find out if the hypothetical "lines crossing" is evident in the data (configurations that produce victory from the expected player given the conditions of the engagement). We don't need to do a large batch of thousands of "runs" and then analyze the data, I think it'd be much faster to iteratively try small things, check the output, and tune repetatively.
